metadata.title: Michael Mayer Still Worth Stashing Despite Quiet Week 7
metadata.description: Las Vegas Raiders tight end Michael Mayer has recorded 31 receptions for 298 yards and a touchdown through seven games. Mayer surpassed 80 receiving yards against Kansas City in Week 4 and Buffalo in Week 6 before cooling off with three catches for 32 yards against the Rams on Sunday. He played 82% of the offensive snaps in Week 7, as Las Vegas continues using both Mayer and Brock Bowers in multiple-tight-end formations. Mayer has enough opportunity to warrant a roster spot even with Bowers healthy, but his inconsistent targets make him a risky Week 8 starter against the Jets.

metadata.title: Michael Mayer catches three passes in Week 7
metadata.description: Michael Mayer caught all three of his targets for 32 yards in the Raiders' 35-21 loss to the Rams in Week 7.
metadata.analysis: Mayer has seen inconsistent involvement in the Las Vegas passing attack of late, receiving three targets or less in three of his last five contests. The tight end remains difficult to trust in all formats as long as Brock Bowers remains healthy, with a Week 8 contest against the New York Jets up next.

metadata.title: Michael Mayer - Three catches in Week 7 loss
metadata.description: Mayer caught all three targets for 32 yards in Sunday's 35-21 loss to the Rams.
metadata.analysis: After a big Week 6 in which Mayer caught seven of nine targets for 95 yards against the Bills, Mayer faded into the background against Los Angeles, as Tre Tucker (5-103-1 receiving), Brock Bowers (6-73-0) and Ashton Jeanty (8-61-1) accounted for most of the production in the passing game for the Raiders. Mayer will be a fantasy TE1/2 for next Sunday's game against the Jets.

metadata.title: Michael Mayer a Streaming Option in Week 7
metadata.description: Las Vegas Raiders tight end Michael Mayer keeps proving he has fantasy value as his team prepares to face a tough Los Angeles Rams defense. Mayer had seven catches for 95 yards in Week 6, topping Brock Bowers' production for the day. The Rams defense ranks second overall against the air game, allowing just 167 passing yards per game and eight passing TDs across six games. Bowers should shoulder the workload, but Mayer should see his fair share of targets since the Raiders' receiving corps is so unpredictable. Vegas' TE2 is a viable streaming option for Week 7.

metadata.title: Michael Mayer Emerging as a Viable Waiver-Wire Target
metadata.description: Las Vegas Raiders tight end Michael Mayer bounced back from a disappointing outing in Week 5 with a strong game in Week 6, recording seven catches for 95 yards on nine targets against the Buffalo Bills. Mayer has now logged at least seven catches and 80 receiving yards in two of his last three games, and he's racked up 28 catches for 266 yards and a touchdown on 34 targets across six games this season. While Mayer is the TE2 on his own team behind Brock Bowers, Las Vegas' tendency to deploy two tight end formations allows both players to be productive. The Raiders are also lacking high-end production from their wide receiver corps, which should allow for Mayer to keep seeing an elevated target share. In leagues where Mayer is available on the waiver wire, he could be a worthy waiver wire target for fantasy managers.

metadata.title: Michael Mayer hauls in seven passes Sunday
metadata.description: Michael Mayer hauled in 7-of-9 targets for 95 yards in Sunday's 33-30 loss to the Buffalo Bills.
metadata.analysis: Mayer had a great performance on Sunday. He set a new career high in receiving yards against the Bills, racking up 95 on his seven catches, which left him with a great fantasy total. He may have some good games here or there moving forward, but he's unlikely to be a reliable week-to-week asset with TE Brock Bowers still easily ahead of him in the pecking order at this point.

metadata.title: Michael Mayer - Outpaces Bowers in loss
metadata.description: Mayer brought in seven of nine targets for 95 yards in the Raiders' 33-30 loss to the Bills on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Mayer set a new single-game career high in receiving yards while outpacing position mate Brock Bowers by 25 yards in the high-scoring loss. Mayer's reception total was a team high for Las Vegas on the afternoon and served as the fourth-year pro's second best of the season. There clearly appears to be consistent room for both athletic tight ends in head coach Klint Kubiak's offense, especially with the Raiders' receiving corps lacking some depth and experience behind Tre Tucker.

metadata.title: Michael Mayer Outproduces All-Pro Teammate in Week 6
metadata.description: Las Vegas Raiders tight end Michael Mayer stepped up big time for this offense during Sunday's game against the Buffalo Bills. Mayer posted a dud last week, but came alive once again this weekend. He hauled in seven of his nine targets for 95 yards in the loss to the Bills. Brock Bowers struggled to find success early in the game, but luckily, Mayer stepped up and made some big plays for this offense. The 95 receiving yards were a season-high for Mayer. He is becoming a more trustworthy fantasy option and is someone worth looking at for next week's matchup against the Los Angeles Rams.

metadata.title: Michael Mayer Offers Streaming Upside vs. Bills
metadata.description: Las Vegas Raiders tight end Michael Mayer has probably hit the waiver wire in your league, but he still has some fantasy value as the Silver and Black gear up to host the Buffalo Bills in Week 6. Mayer's target share and production have taken an expected dip since Brock Bowers returned to the gridiron, and the TE2 had just one catch for two yards in a 45-17 Week 5 loss to the New England Patriots. However, the former second-round pick from Notre Dame also ranks in the top 20 in targets and receiving yards among tight ends. The Bills are allowing 280.4 passing yards per game, so Kirk Cousins could vary his targets in Week 6. Mayer is a streaming option in deep leagues.

metadata.title: Michael Mayer Remains in the Streaming Conversation
metadata.description: Las Vegas Raiders tight end Michael Mayer caught only one pass for two yards in the team's Week 5 blowout loss to the Patriots, and he could hit waiver wires in Week 6 as a reactionary drop. While by no means an every-week starter, Mayer remains fantasy viable while still holding rare insurance value at the position. The Patriots came into the week as one of the most difficult fantasy matchups for tight ends and were able to limit Mayer more than All-Pro Brock Bowers, who has been used more as a large wide receiver through his three healthy games. That said, Mayer is still in the top 20 in targets and receiving yards among tight ends and will remain a streaming option against more favorable opponents. He is RotoBaller's TE23 ahead of a Week 6 matchup with the Bills.

metadata.title: Michael Mayer - One target in blowout loss
metadata.description: Mayer caught his only target for two yards during Sunday's 45-17 loss to the Patriots.
metadata.analysis: Mayer went from having 10 targets in the team's Week 4 loss to Kansas City to a season-low one target versus New England. Fellow tight end Brock Bowers (10) recorded double-digit targets for the third straight contest, and the Las Vegas passing attack funnels through him primarily. With a potential quarterback change from Kirk Cousins to Fernando Mendoza on the horizon, Mayer's outlook moving forward is uncertain.

metadata.title: Michael Mayer disappears in Week 5 loss
metadata.description: Michael Mayer caught his lone target for two yards in a loss to the Patriots.
metadata.analysis: Mayer's one target set a new season low for the 25-year-old tight end. With Brock Bowers continuing to dominate the target share, Mayer is tough to trust in Week 6 against Buffalo.

metadata.title: Michael Mayer Should Get Involved in Week 5 vs. Patriots
metadata.description: Las Vegas Raiders tight end Michael Mayer still has some flex appeal in Week 5 as his team readies to play the Patriots in New England. Even with Brock Bowers healthy and dominating the target share, Mayer has 20 receptions for 160 yards and one touchdown as Vegas' TE2. That includes a season-high eight receptions for 82 yards in a 30-27 loss to the Chiefs in Week 4. The Patriots rank 4th in the league against the pass with just 189.8 yards allowed per game, which could force Kirk Cousins to find more targets in Week 5 outside of Bowers. Plus, Vegas' receiving corps will be missing Jalen Nailor (concussion) and Jack Bech (forearm) on Sunday, while Tre Tucker remains inconsistent from week to week. Mayer is a good waiver-wire target in deep leagues given his continued production.

metadata.title: Michael Mayer A Key Waiver Target Despite Teammate's Return
metadata.description: Las Vegas Raiders tight end Michael Mayer caught eight passes for 82 yards on 10 targets in a close Week 4 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs. That's more involvement than we've ever seen the third-year tight end have in a game where he shared the field with TE Brock Bowers. The concussion injury to Raiders WR Jalen Nailor (head) likely played a part in this, but Mayer's performance was impressive nonetheless. Las Vegas' head coach, Klint Kubiak, indicated that he'd like to get both his tight ends involved in the passing game. Mayer has excellent value for a tight end that's just seven percent rostered in Yahoo leagues, as he caught three passes for 32 yards and a touchdown last week. We could be in the midst of his breakout, in which case it would be exceedingly difficult to pick him up in a few weeks. Finding weekly productive players at the TE position is rare, especially when they were largely undrafted in fantasy leagues, so Mayer should be added in all leagues with 12 or more teams ahead of Week 5.

metadata.title: Michael Mayer goes for 82 yards in Week 4
metadata.description: Michael Mayer caught eight of his 10 targets for 82 yards in a 30-27 loss to the Chiefs in Week 4.
metadata.analysis: Mayer finished second on the team in receiving behind only Brock Bowers. His involvement alongside Bowers has been encouraging as Mayer caught a touchdown back in Week 3. Mayer is worth a look as a tight end streamer in deeper fantasy leagues going forward. He will face the Patriots in Week 5.

metadata.title: Michael Mayer - Eight catches in Week 4 loss
metadata.description: Mayer caught eight of 10 targets for 82 yards in Sunday's 30-27 loss to the Chiefs.
metadata.analysis: Mayer led the Raiders in catches while finishing four receiving yards and one target shy of Brock Bowers' team-high totals. Kirk Cousins has relied heavily on his tight ends in the passing game, and even third-stringer Ian Thomas got in on the fun with a 27-yard touchdown catch in the first quarter. Bowers will continue to lead the position group in Week 5 against the Patriots, but Mayer remains an integral part of Vegas' offense as well.

metadata.title: Michael Mayer Unlikely to Move the Needle in Week 4
metadata.description: Las Vegas Raiders tight end Michael Mayer is still getting targeted by Kirk Cousins, but Brock Bowers' return will cap his production against a tough Kansas City Chiefs defense in Week 4. Mayer was still on the field for over 70% of passing plays in Week 3 and caught a touchdown, but had just three receptions for 32 yards. Even with wide receiver Jack Bech (forearm) out for at least four games, Klint Kubiak's air attack will run through Bowers against a Chiefs passing defense that is allowing just 178.3 yards per game. Unless Bowers is sidelined again, Mayer doesn't produce enough week to week to move the needle in redraft fantasy leagues.

metadata.title: Michael Mayer hauls in touchdown Sunday
metadata.description: Michael Mayer caught 3-of-3 targets for 32 yards and a touchdown in the Raiders 35-27 win over the Saints on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Mayer still made an impact despite the return of Brock Bowers. It was tight end day in New Orleans as the two teams combined for six touchdowns scored by tight ends.

metadata.title: Michael Mayer - Finds end zone in Bowers' return
metadata.description: Mayer caught all three of his targets for 32 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 35-27 win over the Saints.
metadata.analysis: Brock Bowers made his season debut after recovering from minor knee surgery and made an immediate statement with a 10-116-1 line on 13 targets, but Mayer didn't vanish completely from the game plan as a receiver and hauled in his first score of the year in the second quarter. The three targets were still a season low for Mayer, after he compiled a 9-55-0 line on 11 looks from Kirk Cousins during Bowers' absence. As long as Bowers remains healthy, Mayer will struggle to make a consistent impact.

metadata.title: Michael Mayer - Back to No. 2 role Sunday
metadata.description: Mayer is projected to return to a No. 2 role in Sunday's game against the Saints due to Brock Bowers (knee) being ruled active for the contest.
metadata.analysis: Mayer filled in for his star teammate over the first two games of the season, serving as a solid complementary option for Kirk Cousins while generating a 9-55-0 line on 11 targets. However, Bowers' availability Sunday naturally relegates Mayer back to his customary backup role, one in which he may find targets hard to come by against New Orleans.

metadata.title: Michael Mayer's Fantasy Value Hinges on Teammate Returning
metadata.description: Las Vegas Raiders tight end Michael Mayer is coming off a quiet Week 2 performance, and his impact in Week 3 greatly hinges on whether Brock Bowers (knee) makes his season debut. Mayer was a solid fill-in for Bowers in Week 1 when he caught six of seven targets for 32 yards against the Miami Dolphins, then saw less action in Week 2 and tallied just three receptions on four targets for 23 yards. It isn't readily clear who new quarterback Kirk Cousins' preferred targets are, though receivers like Tre Tucker and Jack Bech will likely get more looks if Bowers stays out another week. Mayers' status as a streaming option is strongly tied to whether Bowers plays, which fantasy managers need to keep an eye on ahead of Sunday's road battle against the New Orleans Saints.

metadata.title: Michael Mayer Is Only a Short-Term Streaming Option
metadata.description: Las Vegas Raiders tight end Michael Mayer has filled in for Brock Bowers (knee) without doing much to force his way into fantasy lineups. Mayer caught six passes for 32 yards in Week 1, then followed with three receptions for 23 yards against the Chargers, giving him nine catches for 55 yards through two games. The bigger issue is Bowers' return. Head coach Klint Kubiak said Monday that Bowers will practice this week after missing the first two games, and he had already returned to a limited practice last Friday. If Bowers sits again, Mayer can still be used as a short-term streamer against New Orleans. If Bowers is cleared, Mayer becomes much harder to hold outside deeper formats. RotoBaller's Week 3 tight end waiver article still lists Mayer among the options to add, but its cut list also has him as a drop in most leagues. That split makes sense. Mayer's value right now depends almost entirely on whether Bowers needs another week.

metadata.title: Michael Mayer catches three passes Sunday
metadata.description: Michael Mayer caught 3-of-4 targets for 23 yards in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
metadata.analysis: Sunday's game brought less involvement for Mayer, as he had half of the receptions that he had in the season opener a week before. He was only able to rack up 23 yards over the course of the afternoon, and now he is set to once again be an irrelevant fantasy option with Brock Bowers (knee) soon to make his return to the lineup.

metadata.title: Michael Mayer - Three grabs in Week 2 upset
metadata.description: Mayer brought in three of four targets for 23 yards in the Raiders' 26-14 win over the Chargers on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Mayer served as the No. 1 tight end for the second straight game to open the season due to Brock Bowers' (knee) absence. Mayer played a complementary and mostly short-area role as expected, but through his two starts, he's posted a serviceable a 9-55-0 line on 11 targets. Bowers reportedly could be healthy enough to play in a Week 3 road matchup against the Saints, a development that would relegate Mayer to his usual No. 2 role.

metadata.title: Michael Mayer a Strong Streaming Option on Sunday vs. Chargers
metadata.description: Las Vegas Raiders tight end Michael Mayer has big shoes to fill yet again in Week 2 against the host Los Angeles Chargers. With Brock Bowers (knee) doubtful to play on Sunday, Mayer inherits the TE1 role against a Bolts pass rush that allowed just 179.9 passing yards per game in 2025. Mayer was efficient in Week 1, catching six of seven targets and converting three first downs against the Miami Dolphins, though he logged just 32 yards and no touchdowns. Injuries have peppered the Notre Dame product's NFL career, and he has yet to play a full season since entering the league in 2023. However, his chemistry with new starting quarterback Kirk Cousins could lead to even more targets in Week 2. This is Mayer's opportunity to boost his production in Bowers' absence, making him a viable streaming option.

metadata.title: Michael Mayer a Top Week 2 Streamer if he Starts Again
metadata.description: Las Vegas Raiders tight end Michael Mayer took advantage of the starting job in Sunday's 27-13 win over Miami, catching six passes for 32 yards with Brock Bowers sidelined following a meniscus procedure. The yardage wasn't much, but six catches are enough to get attention at tight end. Mayer has done this before when the Raiders needed more from him. In the four games he played without Bowers last season, he totaled 18 receptions for 196 yards, accounting for more than half of his season production in both categories. Las Vegas also signed Mayer to a multi-year extension just before the opener. His Week 2 appeal now comes down largely to Bowers' availability. Bowers was initially expected to miss a game or two, so another start against the Chargers remains possible. If Bowers sits again, Mayer belongs near the top of the tight end streaming options on the waiver wire. His short-term fantasy value drops quickly once Bowers returns.

metadata.title: Michael Mayer hauls in six receptions in Week 1 win
metadata.description: Michael Mayer hauled in six of his seven targets for 32 yards in the Raiders' 27-13 Week 1 win over the Miami Dolphins.
metadata.analysis: Mayer took advantage of the absence of No. 1 tight end Brock Bowers, leading the team in targets in the win. The tight end remains a steady option as long as Bowers remains sidelined for fantasy managers, with a Week 2 matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers ahead.

metadata.title: Michael Mayer - Six catches in top TE role
metadata.description: Mayer brought in six of seven targets for 32 yards in the Raiders' 27-13 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Filling the No. 1 tight end role with Brock Bowers (knee) sidelined, Mayer set the pace for the Raiders in targets while also tying for the team lead in receptions. Mayer gained 14 of his yards on one catch, so he was mired in an extreme short-area role for the majority of the afternoon. Nevertheless, he's proven capable of offering useful production as Bowers' fill-in on multiple occasions, although Mayer could revert to his usual reserve role in light of reports that Bowers could be ready for his season debut as early as next Sunday's Week 2 road matchup against the Chargers.

metadata.title: Michael Mayer a Worthy Start in Favorable Week 1 Matchup
metadata.description: Las Vegas Raiders tight end Michael Mayer played a limited role as a receiver in 2025, recording 35 catches for 328 yards and one touchdown on 50 targets across 13 games. However, with Raiders TE1 Brock Bowers (knee) sidelined, Mayer could step into an elevated target share in the Raiders' 2026 season opener against the Miami Dolphins. Across four games with Bowers inactive in 2025, Mayer recorded 18 catches for 196 yards and a touchdown on 24 targets. While his numbers may not leap off the page, Las Vegas should field an improved passing game with new head coach Klint Kubiak calling plays in 2026. The Dolphins also profile as a favorable matchup on paper for Mayer, as Miami allowed the fifth-most fantasy points to tight ends last season. All in all, Mayer projects as a low-end top-12 tight end option for fantasy managers in Week 1.

metadata.title: Michael Mayer agrees to a three-year, $45 million deal with Raiders
metadata.description: Michael Mayer has agreed to a three-year, $45 million deal with the Las Vegas Raiders.
metadata.analysis: Mayer is an all around contributor, making it well worth the investment for the Raiders. For fantasy, it means that he is behind Brock Bowers for the long term, but maybe the Raiders will employ more tight end sets so both can eat, as they are likely the two most talented pass catchers on the team at this point in time. Time will tell what his fantasy value will become.

metadata.title: Michael Mayer - Gets three-year extension with Las Vegas
metadata.description: Mayer signed a three-year, $45 million contract extension with the Raiders on Saturday, Ian Rapoport of NFL.com reports.
metadata.analysis: The deal includes $30 million guaranteed, and the $15 million APY ranks fourth among current tight ends. Mayer has operated as the Raiders' TE2 for the past couple of seasons, but the fourth-year pro is expected to operate in an expanded role Sunday against the Dolphins in the absence of Brock Bowers, who is expected to miss at least one or two games after undergoing a meniscus trim procedure Tuesday. Mayer finished the 2025 regular season with 35 catches (on 50 targets) for 328 yards and a touchdown across 13 games.
